probes.question: True or false: the attentional blink means people can never see a second target in a fast stream.
In the stream B, X, C, K with targets X and K, which target is often missed?

image.alt: A brightly lit funfair Ferris wheel at night, its spinning lights blurred into blue and white streaks.

body.question: Letters flash rapidly one after another and you must spot two targets, X and K. You catch the X. When is a second target K most likely to be missed?
options: About 200 to 500 milliseconds after the X
Only if K comes before the X
body.reveal: People struggle to notice a second target that appears 200 to 500 milliseconds after the first and is followed by distractions. This is the attentional blink. It is thought to come from a two-stage visual system: everything gets some processing, but only salient items get in-depth processing.
